arxiv-2201-07398.title: An efficient Chorin-Temam projection proper orthogonal decomposition based reduced-order model for nonstationary Stokes equations
arxiv-2201-07398.creator: Xi Li, Yan Luo, Minfu Feng
arxiv-2201-07398.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xi Li, Yan Luo, Minfu Feng. In this paper, we propose an efficient proper orthogonal decomposition based reduced-order model(POD-ROM) for nonstationary Stokes equations, which combines the classical projection method with POD technique. This new scheme mainly owns two advantages: the first one is low computational costs since the classical projection method decouples the reduced-order velocity variable and reduced-order pressure variable, and POD technique further improves the computational efficiency; the second advantage consists of circumventing the verification of classical LBB/inf-sup condition for mixed POD spaces

arxiv-2207-04942.title: A high sensitivity tool for geophysical applications: A geometrically locked Ring Laser Gyroscope. Journal: osajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2207-04942.creator: E. Maccioni, \authormark 1,2 N. Beverini, \authormark 1 G. Carelli, \authormark 1,2,* G. Di Somma, \authormark 1,2 A. Di Virgilio, \authormark 2 and P. Marsili \authormark 1,2
arxiv-2207-04942.description: Abstract This work demonstrates that a middle size ring laser gyroscope (RLG) can be a very sensitive and robust instrument for rotational seismology, even if it operates in a quite noisy environment. The RLG has a square cavity, 1.60 × 1.60 1.60\times 1.60 m 2 , and it lies in a plane orthogonal to the Earth rotational axis.

arxiv-2308-09495.title: Understanding X-ray absorption in liquid water: triple excitations in multilevel coupled cluster theory
arxiv-2308-09495.creator: Sarai Dery Folkestad, Alexander C. Paul, Regina Paul (née Matveeva), Sonia Coriani, Michael Odelius, Marcella Iannuzzi, Henrik Koch
arxiv-2308-09495.description: Abstract We present the first successful application of the coupled cluster approach to simulate the X-ray absorption (XA) spectrum of liquid water. The system size limitations of standard coupled cluster theory are overcome by employing a newly developed coupled cluster method for large molecular systems.

arxiv-2310-02192.title: Sneaked references: Cooked reference metadata inflate citation counts
arxiv-2310-02192.creator: Lonni Besançon, Guillaume Cabanac, Cyril Labbé, Alexander Magazinov
arxiv-2310-02192.description: Abstract We report evidence of an undocumented method to manipulate citation counts involving ‘sneaked’ references. Sneaked references are registered as metadata for scientific articles in which they do not appear. This manipulation exploits trusted relationships between various actors: publishers, the Crossref metadata registration agency, digital libraries, and bibliometric platforms.

arxiv-2407-13654.title: All-optical Loss-tolerant Distributed Quantum Sensing
arxiv-2407-13654.creator: Rajveer Nehra 1,2,3,4, Changhun Oh 5,6, Liang Jiang 5, Alireza Marandi 1
arxiv-2407-13654.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Rajveer Nehra 1,2,3,4, Changhun Oh 5,6, Liang Jiang 5, Alireza Marandi 1. Distributed quantum sensing (DQS) leverages quantum resources to estimate an unknown global property of a networked quantum sensor beyond the classical limit. We propose and analyze an all-optical resource-efficient scheme for the next-generation DQS systems. Our method utilizes phase-sensitive optical parametric amplifiers (OPAs) and linear interferometers and achieves the sensitivity close to the optimal limit, as determined by the quantum Fisher information of the entangled resource state.

arxiv-2410-01204.title: p– ϕ \phi femtoscopic correlation analysis using a dynamical model
arxiv-2410-01204.creator: \firstname Kenshi \lastname Kuroki \fnsep, \firstname Tetsufumi \lastname Hirano \fnsep
arxiv-2410-01204.description: Abstract We analyse the p– ϕ \phi correlation functions in high-multiplicity proton+proton collisions at the LHC using a dynamical model, DCCI2, and discuss the effects of collision dynamics on the p– ϕ \phi femtoscopic study. Collision dynamics, such as collective expansion and hadronic rescatterings, leads to the relative momentum-dependent non-Gaussian source functions.

arxiv-2507-12003.title: Expanding ML-Documentation Standards For Better Security
arxiv-2507-12003.creator: 1 st Cara Ellen Appel
arxiv-2507-12003.description: Abstract This article presents the current state of ML-security and of the documentation of ML-based systems, models and datasets in research and practice based on an extensive review of the existing literature. It shows a generally low awareness of security aspects among ML-practitioners and organizations and an often unstandardized approach to documentation, leading to overall low quality of ML-documentation.

arxiv-2509-23179.title: A Near-Cache Architectural Framework for Cryptographic Computing
arxiv-2509-23179.creator: Jingyao Zhang, Elaheh Sadredini
arxiv-2509-23179.description: Abstract Recent advancements in post-quantum cryptographic algorithms have led to their standardization by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to safeguard information security in the post-quantum era. These algorithms, however, employ public keys and signatures that are 3 to 9 × \times longer than those used in pre-quantum cryptography, resulting in significant performance and energy efficiency overheads.

arxiv-2601-04100.title: Quantifying the Impact of Modules and Their Interactions in the PSO -X Framework
arxiv-2601-04100.creator: Christian L. Camacho-Villalón, Ana Nikolikj, Katharina Dost, Eva Tuba, Sašo Džeroski, Tome Eftimov
arxiv-2601-04100.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Christian L. Camacho-Villalón, Ana Nikolikj, Katharina Dost, Eva Tuba, Sašo Džeroski, Tome Eftimov. The PSO -X framework incorporates dozens of modules that have been proposed for solving single-objective continuous optimization problems using particle swarm optimization. While modular frameworks enable users to automatically generate and configure algorithms tailored to specific optimization problems, the complexity of this process increases with the number of modules in the framework and the degrees of freedom defined for their interaction.

pmc-10617981.title: SND1 binds SARS-CoV-2 negative-sense RNA and promotes viral RNA synthesis through NSP9
pmc-10617981.creator: Nora Schmidt, Sabina Ganskih, Yuanjie Wei, Alexander Gabel, Sebastian Zielinski, Hasmik Keshishian, Caleb A. Lareau, Liv Zimmermann, Jana Makroczyova, Cadence Pearce, Karsten Krey, Thomas Hennig, Sebastian Stegmaier, Lambert Moyon, Marc Horlacher, Simone Werner, Jens Aydin, Marco Olguin-Nava, Ramya
pmc-10617981.description: SummaryRegulation of viral RNA biogenesis is fundamental to productive SARS-CoV-2 infection. To characterize host RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) involved in this process, we biochemically identified proteins bound to genomic and subgenomic SARS-CoV-2 RNAs. We find that the host protein SND1 binds the 5′ end of negative-sense viral RNA and is required for SARS-CoV-2 RNA synthesis.

pmc-10657875.title: Microbiota of maize kernels as influenced by Aspergillus flavus infection in susceptible and resistant inbreds
pmc-10657875.creator: Geromy G. Moore, Subbaiah Chalivendra, Brian M. Mack, Matthew K. Gilbert, Jeffrey W. Cary, Kanniah Rajasekaran
pmc-10657875.description: BackgroundNearly everything on Earth harbors a microbiome. A microbiome is a community of microbes (bacteria, fungi, and viruses) with potential to form complex networks that involve mutualistic and antagonistic interactions. Resident microbiota on/in an organism are determined by the external environment, both biotic and abiotic, and the intrinsic adaptability of each organism.

pmc-11494217.title: Insights into undergraduate medical student selection tools: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11494217.creator: Pin-Hsiang Huang, Arash Arianpoor, Silas Taylor, Jenzel Gonzales, Boaz Shulruf
pmc-11494217.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeEvaluating medical school selection tools is vital for evidence-based student selection. With previous reviews revealing knowledge gaps, this meta-analysis offers insights into the effectiveness of these selection tools.MethodsA systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted applying the following criteria: peer-reviewed articles available in English, published from 2010 and which include empirical data linking performance in selection tools with assessment and dropout outcomes of undergraduate entry medical programs. Systematic reviews, meta-analyses, general opinion pieces, or commentaries were excluded.

pmc-11652705.title: The Influence of Gentrification on Adverse Birth Outcomes in California
pmc-11652705.creator: Xing Gao, Mahasin S Mujahid, Amani M Nuru-Jeter, Rachel Morello-Frosch
pmc-11652705.description: Evidence has documented the effects of place on perinatal outcomes, but less is known about the sociopolitical mechanisms, such as gentrification, that shape neighborhood context and produce spatialized inequities in adverse birth outcomes. Leveraging a diverse sample in California, we assessed the associations between gentrification and birth outcomes: preterm birth, small-for-gestational-age, and low birth weight.

pmc-12533463.title: Hard then, harder now: internal medicine residents’ moral distress pre and amidst COVID-19
pmc-12533463.creator: Harriet Fisher, Stephanie McLaughlin, Tavinder Ark, Sondra Zabar, Katharine Lawrence, Kathleen Hanley
pmc-12533463.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundMoral distress, which occurs when the ethically correct action cannot be taken because of internal or external constraints, is associated with depression, burnout, and the desire to leave the healthcare profession among healthcare workers.

pmc-13001301.title: Quantitative evaluation of the topographical maps of three-dimensional choroidal vascularity index in gestational diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional observational study
pmc-13001301.creator: Ligang Jiang, Yimei Ji, Xin Jiang, Yune Zhao
pmc-13001301.description: BackgroundGestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) may be associated with occult abnormalities in choroidal microcirculation.This study utilizes ultra-widefield swept-source OCTA (SS-OCTA) and introduces the three-dimensional choroidal vascularity index (3D-CVI) as a volumetric quantitative parameter to systematically characterize the choroidal microcirculatory characteristics in GDM.MethodsThis cross-sectional study utilized SS-OCTA with a 24 × 20 mm scan range.

pmc-13057108.title: Most purported brain-released plasma circular RNAs detected in stroke likely originate from white blood cells
pmc-13057108.creator: Grant C O’Connell, Kara Williams, Rachel A Boyette, Jing Wang
pmc-13057108.description: The identification and development of reliable acute stroke blood biomarkers could limit life-threatening delays stemming from mistriage. Recent investigations have reported a set of 24 plasma circRNAs believed to be released from the brain into circulation during acute ischemic events with potential to serve as such biomarkers.

pmc-13292246.title: Utility of bronchial blocker placement in the lateral versus supine position for thoracoscopic surgery: a randomised controlled trial in China
pmc-13292246.creator: Rongjun Liu, Renli Wang, Xizhen Liu, Fanfu Zeng, Junping Chen, Jianliang Sun, Xiaoyu Li, Bo Lu
pmc-13292246.description: SummaryBackgroundBronchial blocker (BB) displacement after supine placement and subsequent patient repositioning remains a significant challenge during video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS). We aimed to test the hypothesis that placing the BB in the lateral decubitus position after standard supine tracheal intubation would reduce the incidence of malposition compared to conventional supine placement.

pmc-13475625.title: Knowledge–Behavior and Adherence Gap in Protective Eyewear Use Among Outdoor Workers with High Ocular Surface Disease Burden in a Desert Environment
pmc-13475625.creator: Saeed Aljohani, Mohammed Suliman Alomari
pmc-13475625.description: ObjectiveOutdoor workers’ ocular health in harsh environments is often overlooked, despite their heightened risk of eye disease. This study aimed to examine knowledge of sun-related ocular hazards and adherence to protective eyewear use among outdoor workers in a desert environment, and to contextualize these behaviors against objective ocular surface findings.
